title: Height
definition: Utilities for setting the height of an element, including fixed heights, percentage heights, and viewport heights.
simpleExplanation: How tall something is. Just like width, you can use the spacing scale (`h-16`), percentages (`h-full`), or viewport units (`h-screen`).
realWorldExample: Creating a 'Hero Image' at the top of a landing page that perfectly takes up the entire vertical space of the user's monitor using `h-screen`.

basic: If you apply `h-full` to a child, but the parent `div` doesn't have a defined height, what happens?
intermediate: What modern Tailwind class accounts for the mobile browser address bar popping in and out?

answers.question: Parent has no height?
answers.answer: `h-full` will do nothing. Percentage heights ONLY work if the parent has an explicitly defined height.

answers.question: Mobile address bar?
answers.answer: `h-dvh` (Dynamic Viewport Height). It automatically resizes the height when the mobile Safari/Chrome address bar expands or shrinks.
